A volt politikus vasárnap részt vett az eXtremeMan triatlonversenyen, ahol úszás közben rosszul lett, és már nem tudták újraéleszteni. Velkey Gábor 63 éves volt, a legrégebbi magyarországi ironman triatlonversenyt többször is teljesítette. A verseny szervezői vasárnap közölték, hogy a parttól mintegy 100 méterre rosszul lett az egyik résztvevő, hamar kimentették a vízből, de az összehangolt, szakszerű ellátás során nem tudták megmenteni a versenyző életét. A szervezők a helyszínen tájékoztatták a családot, és közleményükben is együttérzésüket fejezték, ki. A 444 azt írja, szociológus, főiskolai docens és középiskolai tanár dr. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/a.text: Donald Trump said he was issuing the demand for war reparations in response to Iranian negotiators making claims for the damages from the five-month war. Photograph: Jacquelyn Martin/AP View image in fullscreen Donald Trump said he was issuing the demand for war reparations in response to Iranian negotiators making claims for the damages from the five-month war. Photograph: Jacquelyn Martin/AP Iran Trump demands Iran pay compensation for decades of US soldier deaths US president’s statement is latest sign that negotations to end war and reopen strait of Hormuz have stalled Andrew Roth in Washington Mon 10 Aug 2026 16.45 EDT Last modified on Mon 10 Aug 2026 17.15 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Donald Trump has said he will demand that Iran pay compensation for the deaths of thousands of US soldiers and Iran’s own civilians killed in recent decades in the latest sign his negotiations to end the war and reopen the strait of Hormuz have reached an impasse. The US president is trying to end conflicts in Iran , Gaza and Lebanon, and his additional demands of Iran are likely to provoke anger in Tehran at the same time as Israel has rejected Trump’s terms for a 15-point roadmap to end the war in Gaza. In a post on Truth Social, Trump said he was issuing the demand for war reparations in response to Iranian negotiators making similar claims for damages for the five-month war that has killed thousands and devastated Iran’s military and economy. Iran issues tough demands to reopen strait of Hormuz as deal still out of reach Read more “Now I am likewise demanding compensation from Iran, for all of the people that they have killed and gravely wounded with their roadside bombs and many conflicts, for which they are famous, as led initially by Gen Soleimani, including the families of those killed on the USS Cole, and thousands of others killed in combat,” he wrote on Truth Social. “Additionally, compensation should be paid to the families of the hundreds of thousands of innocent protesters that Iran has killed over the last 50 years, not to mention the 52,000 that have been killed in the last five months.” The demands are likely to be a nonstarter for Iran’s leaders in the careful peace negotiations aimed at reopening the strait of Hormuz, through which 20% of global oil trade flowed before the US and Israel launched joint strikes on Iran in late February. Trump and other senior negotiators have claimed many times that a deal is imminent, although none has materialised. The remarks followed a series of setbacks for Trump’s efforts to end several Middle East conflicts before the midterm elections in November, in which high oil prices and inflation will probably hurt fellow Republicans at the polls. On Sunday, the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, said he rejected the Trump-backed Board of Peace’s 15-point plan to end Israel’s war in Gaza . Netanyahu had said Hamas must fully disarm before Israel would consider pulling out of Gaza, rather than the phased withdrawal proposed by the Board of Peace. Netanyahu framed the decision as a rejection of US pressure on Israel to make peace in several wars in the Middle East. “Unlike all those who lecture us, we do what needs to be done for Israel’s security, and we can and know how to stand our ground, even against our best friends when necessary,” Netanyahu said. Iran plots to deal Trump a blow in midterms by keeping him entangled in war Read more Trump has not replied to Netanyahu’s statement, which was a remarkably public break between the leaders of the US and its closest ally in the Middle East. But in response to a shouted question in the Oval Office on Monday, he said his relationship with Netanyahu was “very good”. Trump has sought to increase pressure on Iran. An hour after his first post demanding war reparations from Tehran, he broadened their scope to include the victims of recent wars throughout the region. “Also, with respect to the Iran negotiations, Iran should be responsible for the damages and death caused to the people of Lebanon, Syria, Yemen, and Gaza!” he wrote. https://www.nbcnews.com/world/ukraine/ru.text: KYIV, Ukraine — Russia hammered Kyiv with drones in daylight attacks on Wednesday hours before Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with world leaders at the U.N. General Assembly. Two people were killed and 41 wounded in Ukraine’s capital as the attacks stretched into Wednesday afternoon. Palls of black smoke floated above the city following the latest in what have been daily Russian attacks that torment Ukrainian civilians. The drones set off fires and damaged buildings in Kyiv and elsewhere in Ukraine overnight, authorities said. Zelenskyy was in New York for the annual U.N. gathering as part of his diplomatic effort to shore up and recruit further international support for his country’s grueling 4½-year fight against Russia’s invasion. He addressed the General Assembly, met with European leaders and was also due to hold talks with NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte. In his address to the Assembly, Zelenskyy urged the international community to keep limiting Russian oil revenues to prevent Russia’s ability to keep financing its war in Ukraine. “When someone gives Russia more money through trade, they give this war more time. And that is exactly why we insist on limiting trade with the aggressor, and why we are burning Russia’s revenues ourselves,” he said. Zelenskyy met on Tuesday with U.S. President Donald Trump, who has shown impatience with the lack of progress in talks aimed at ending the war and the escalating aerial attacks by both sides this year. Russia’s President Vladimir Putin hasn’t traveled to the gathering in years, sending Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov instead. Lavrov, who met with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio to discuss Ukraine and other issues, reaffirmed Wednesday that Moscow is open for talks on ending the conflict in Ukraine, but wouldn’t accept a break in hostilities before a peace deal is agreed. Rubio told reporters on the sidelines of the General Assembly meeting that Trump has invited Putin to the G20 meeting that he will host at his Miami country club in December, adding that “we think it’s an opportunity for him to engage not just with the president, but with other world leaders.” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said that Moscow was grateful for the invitation, adding that the issue will be discussed further via diplomatic channels. Ukraine has hit back at Russia by damaging oil refineries that are a vital pillar of the country’s economy. Speaking in New York, Zelenskyy said that “our target is Russia’s ability to finance this war, to drag it out, to make it more brutal and more destructive. Russia’s finances and Russia’s production are what must be stopped.” The Ukrainian leader said at the start of his U.S. visit that he had proposals for a possible de-escalation in the war. Urgent issues for Kyiv are halting devastating Russian strikes on Ukraine’s power grid and ensuring Ukrainian grain can be shipped to world markets through the Black Sea despite the war. Ukraine also needs more U.S.-made Patriot air defense systems as a shield against Russian ballistic missiles, but Patriots are in short supply after the war in Iran began. In Zaporizhzhia, in southeastern Ukraine, two men ages 37 and 39 were wounded by a strike that started a large fire at a shopping mall. Emergency services said the fire spread across about 6,000 square meters (1.5 acres) before coming under control. The Russian Defense Ministry said that its forces struck Ukraine’s military-industrial and energy sector facilities, logistics centers and sea vessels in overnight attacks. The ministry said its air defenses intercepted more than 500 Ukrainian drones over multiple Russian regions, as well as illegally annexed Crimea and waters of the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea. In another development, the Polish military said a Russian military helicopter briefly violated Poland’s airspace Wednesday on the country’s border with Russia’s Kaliningrad exclave. It said that “the nature of the incident suggests that Russia is once again testing the readiness of our air defense.”

Photograph: Jewel Samad/AFP/Getty Images First Thing newsletter US news First Thing: Both blocs claim upper hand in crucial Israeli election Benjamin Netanyahu vows to form new coalition while opposition bloc leader says result shows prime minister should step down. Plus, a scathing review of Elon Musk’s AI-generated version of The Odyssey Martin Belam Wed 28 Oct 2026 07.33 EDT Last modified on Wed 28 Oct 2026 07.35 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Good morning. Israel could be in for weeks of political haggling after exit polls and partial official results showed neither Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition nor the opposition bloc led by the former general Gadi Eisenkot had won enough seats to form a government. With 70% of the vote, or 4m ballots, counted so far, the Netanyahu bloc had 54 seats, the Eisenkot-led Change bloc 47 seats, and the Palestinian parties 19 seats. Sixty-one seats are needed for a majority. What have the two leaders said so far? Israel’s longest-serving prime minister vowed to assemble a coalition through agreements between his Likud party, far-right factions and Jewish religious parties. Eisenkot had said earlier in the evening that “people decided in favour of change” and Netanyahu should have “announced today his retirement from politics”. What does the increase in the Palestinian bloc mean? The election was marked by a record participation by Israeli citizens of Palestinian origin, a discriminated minority that makes up about 20% of the country’s population. Julian Borger explains from Nazareth that opposition leader Eisenkot will have to work with Arab-Israeli leaders to have a hope of governing. Millions of other Palestinians living under Israeli rule in the occupied West Bank and Gaza cannot vote. Here is what we know about the declared results so far . Our live coverage continues on the website . Trump says government to ‘terminate’ Biden-era methane emissions rules View image in fullscreen The EPA says the proposal is expected to save $45bn in costs to consumers and businesses. Photograph: Matthew Brown/AP Donald Trump has announced his administration is “terminating” Biden-era regulations holding oil and gas companies accountable for large leaks of planet-warming methane. According to the Environmental Protection Agency, the proposal is expected to save $45bn in costs to consumers and businesses. Last year, the US emitted more methane from its oil and gas sector than any other country in the world. Methane is responsible for at least a quarter of today’s warming. What else has Trump been saying about fossil fuels? Trump suggested on Tuesday that Venezuela would become the 51st US state as the president showed off a tanker he claimed had “1m barrels of oil on it” from the country, nine months after deposing its president. Flávio Bolsonaro flees Brazil after presidential election loss, reports say View image in fullscreen Flávio Bolsonaro at the weekend. Photograph: Lucas Neves/NurPhoto/Shutterstock The far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro has reportedly fled Brazil and is on his way to the United States after losing Sunday’s presidential election to the leftwing incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Bolsonaro allies told the news website Metrópoles that he would land in Florida and planned to request political asylum. “The Trump administration has been informed,” the website added. Brazilian federal police are investigating him for possible involvement in a money-laundering scheme worth about £680m ($905m) involving betting companies. What has re-elected president Lula had to say about Bolsonaro’s exit? He condemned Bolsonaro’s apparent decision to flee. “This is what the family Bolsonaro are like. Brazil is their second homeland. Their first homeland is licking the boots of the US, as he’s become accustomed to doing. The act of leaving Brazil is shameful.” Death toll in Spain train collision rises to 30 A high-speed train collision south of Madrid killed has killed at least 30 people, according to regional authorities, as Spain reels from its second such disaster this year. A collision between two high-speed trains in southern Spain in January resulted in the deaths of 46 people. Read the full report here and live blog here . Oleshky truce appears to hold as two European leaders have ‘frank’ call with Putin View image in fullscreen A woman walks beneath anti-drone nets in Oleshky. Photograph: Evgeniy Maloletka/AP A local ceasefire in a southern Ukrainian city under Russian occupation appeared to be holding , with both sides ceasing drone attacks ahead of an apparent evacuation of about 2,000 trapped and desperate civilians. Witnesses reported that the deadly frontline across the river was quiet for the first time in four years. Meanwhile Finland’s president, Alexander Stubb, and Norway’s prime minister, Jonas Gahr Støre, held what they described as a “frank and substantive” phone call with Vladimir Putin. Writing on social media, Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said Russia “must stop dragging out this war” and said he welcomed European attempts to end it. Doctor removes prostate from 35 miles away in first telerobotic surgery in US View image in fullscreen Telesurgery allows surgeons to control robotic instruments remotely. Photograph: Sean Smith/The Guardian A Florida surgeon has performed the first telerobotic operation between two US hospitals, removing the prostate of a man with cancer from 35 miles away, according to officials. Telesurgery allows surgeons to control robotic instruments remotely but researchers are still evaluating its safety, reliability and cybersecurity.
